core.title: Give every plan artifact its canonical identity
core.given: Any plan artifact of a kind the stack recognizes, outside the vendored and generated trees this check never scans, whether new, edited, or existing and unchanged
core.when: the plan set is authored or validated
core.then: The artifact carries its canonical identity for its kind: the identity field the stack assigns to that plan-artifact kind, present, non-empty, and canonical for that artifact (not a placeholder and not another kind's field).
prefer: Add the identity field for the artifact's kind; when you find an existing artifact without one, add it.
Use the same identity in every other plan artifact that references this one.
avoid: Adding a placeholder identity just to pass the check; the identity must be the canonical one others reference.
Using another kind's identity field instead of the one canonical for the artifact's kind.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
core.why: An artifact without an identity cannot be referenced, bound, or traced, and every rule that resolves references silently skips it, so its gaps go unseen.
evidence: Every recognized plan artifact outside the vendored and generated trees this check never scans, including existing unchanged ones, shows the identity field for its kind with a non-placeholder value.
The value is the identity other plan artifacts use to reference it.
The stack's plan-integrity check reports no identity finding for the plan set.
verification: Scope: scan every recognized plan artifact in the plan set, whatever the author and whether new, edited, or existing and unchanged, not only changed ones; kinds the stack does not recognize as plan artifacts are out of scope.

The obligation covers a missing identity field and a present but noncanonical one (empty, placeholder, or another kind's field). The check compares the identity field against the artifact's kind, not merely whether some identity key is present; where the realizing check's coverage of noncanonical values is unspecified, canonicality of a present value is judged by a reviewer.

Vendored and generated trees are never scanned. The exact excluded trees are owned by this check's realization as the check's own exclusion list; they are deliberately not equated with the stack-wide never-scanned list, which is a separate concept and may be broader (substituting it would drop obligations on artifacts outside the check's own exclusions).

Check ordering (after parse, before identity-uniqueness checking) is implementation ordering, not an exemption: an artifact that fails to parse is reported by the parse rule, and it must still carry its identity once it parses.
Strict disposition, severity 3: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Realization details left open: the realizing validator's exact finding format and how it classifies artifact kinds are not fixed by the core; an observer that reports the recognized kind of each plan artifact may need to be added.

values: plan artifact of a kind the stack recognizes
recognized artifact lacks its canonical identity (field absent, empty, or not the canonical identity for its kind)

fires: A plan artifact of a recognized kind is written without its canonical identity field.
A recognized plan artifact is edited and its identity field is removed or left empty.
A recognized plan artifact carries an identity field, but the value is a placeholder or another kind's field rather than its canonical identity.
During plan validation, an existing, unchanged recognized artifact (from any author) is found without its canonical identity.
doesNotFire: The artifact sits under a vendored or generated tree this check never scans.
The artifact's kind is not one the stack recognizes as a plan artifact.

profileRequirements.meaning: For each recognized plan-artifact kind not identified by its own URN, the name of the field in which the artifact declares its canonical identity (the value other plan artifacts reference). Kinds that declare a URN are covered by urn.declaration, not by this key.
profileRequirements.bunValue: train -> train_id, interlocking -> interlocking_id, journey -> journey_id (verifier_detail[1]: 'Recognized identity fields: train_id, interlocking_id, journey_id, urn'; then and evidence[0] name the same four; the `urn` field itself is delivered by urn.declaration)

proposedKeys.meaning: For each recognized plan-artifact kind not identified by its own URN, the name of the field in which the artifact declares its canonical identity (its value is what other plan artifacts reference). Kinds that declare a URN are covered by the existing urn.declaration key, so this key deliberately excludes them.
proposedKeys.bunValue: train -> train_id, interlocking -> interlocking_id, journey -> journey_id (the `urn` field for URN-identified kinds stays with urn.declaration)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.declaration is documented as how a plan artifact declares its own URN - URN declaration syntax only - so it cannot carry the mapping from a non-URN kind to its identity field; urn.<artifact> keys give URN value shapes and urn.binding.<artifact> how source or test files bind to an artifact. No existing key maps a plan-artifact kind such as train, interlocking or journey to the declaration field (train_id, interlocking_id, journey_id) that holds its canonical identity, so only that non-URN mapping is proposed here.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully stack-neutral (a plan artifact must carry the canonical identity of its kind); everything concrete lives in the profile or the realization. The per-kind identity declaration is split across two keys, each kept to its own documented scope: urn.declaration is used only for how a URN-identified plan artifact declares its own URN (the Bun `urn` field), and the non-URN per-kind identity fields (train_id, interlocking_id, journey_id) are covered by no existing key - urn.<artifact> gives URN value shapes and urn.binding.<artifact> how source or test files bind to an artifact - so urn.plan_identity_fields is proposed for exactly that non-URN mapping. The recognized-kind list comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds (bun.json never enumerates the kinds - they are implied by the recognized identity fields and classified by the realizing validator). The exact four excluded trees (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) are this check's own realization-owned exclusion list and stay in bunOnly; core verification describes the checker-owned exclusion scope and deliberately does not equate it with the stack-wide roots.excluded list, which is a separate concept that may be broader - substituting it would drop obligations on recognized artifacts outside the check's own exclusions. The neutral activation-fact vocabulary has no path fact, so the Bun path_glob fact is expressed through unless/doesNotFire plus the realization-owned list, and the core's facts are re-indexed (Bun facts[2] becomes core facts[1]). Kind-specific fires examples (interlocking_id, journey_id, urn) were generalized to the recognized-kind level; the concrete examples remain in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference. Validator and sibling-rule ids (planner_plan_integrity, atdd-bun.planner.parse, atdd-bun.planner.identity-unique) stay bunOnly. Note that even the Bun source does not fix how kinds are classified or how much of the noncanonical case the validator detects; the core keeps that honesty in verification rather than inventing coverage.
